description: Fragment 0 of 2 of a single AES-128-GCM sealed TELEMETRY message (docs/encryption.md sections 2 and 5). The message is sealed ONCE, whole, and only then cut into ESP-NOW sized fragments, so the 16-octet tag lives at the end of fragment 1 and neither fragment can be opened on its own. The AAD is the canonicalized LOGICAL header: FRAGMENTED cleared, fragment_index 0, fragment_count 1, and payload_size set to the full 236-octet ciphertext-and-tag size. Because every field that re-fragmentation changes is excluded from the AAD, the tag is identical no matter how the message was cut, which is what lets a gateway reassemble from one transport and re-fragment onto another without holding the key. btp::decode() does not verify the tag; this vector proves the framing and gives an implementation the exact octets to reassemble and open.

aead.cipher_id_note: CIPHER_ID is bits 2-3 of flags (mask 0x000C). flags=0x0003 is FRAGMENTED|ENCRYPTED with those bits clear, which is the normative encoding for AES-128-GCM.
aead.key_note: Fixed, public, sequential test key (0x00..0x0f), documented only so this vector can be reproduced. NEVER use in production: a real key never travels and is never written down in the clear.
aead.nonce_construction: source_id || boot_id || sequence, each 4 octets little-endian (btp::aead_nonce). Derivable from the frame fields above; spelled out here only for convenience.
aead.aad_construction: The 36 octets btp::encode_header() writes for the CANONICALIZED logical header: version octet 2 because ENCRYPTED is set, flags 0x0002 with FRAGMENTED cleared, payload_size 236 (the whole ciphertext and tag), fragment_index 0, fragment_count 1. This differs from either fragment's own on-wire header, which is the entire point of the canonicalization.
aead.plaintext_note: 220 octets, byte i = (i*7) & 0xFF. Chosen so ciphertext+tag is 236 octets and needs exactly two ESP-NOW fragments (210 + 26).
aead.reproduction_note: sealed = AESGCM(key).encrypt(nonce, plaintext, aad); the library appends the 16-octet tag, matching the logical payload layout required by the logical payload. Fragment 0 is sealed[0:210], fragment 1 is sealed[210:236]. Reassembling the two payloads in index order reproduces `sealed` exactly, and aead_open over the reassembled message must return the plaintext above.
